sample: deliberately selected ten-category sample used during rule tuning

records.review_note: OAuth, bearer transport, developer API keys, and single-account access tokens are documented, but the list conflates credential types with bearer transport and omits current service keys. Developer API keys are limited to documented app-management endpoints rather than serving as general CRM credentials; service keys entered public beta on February 10, 2026 and replace legacy private apps for new system-to-system integrations.
records.correction: OAuth 2.0 for distributed apps; static/legacy private-app access token for one authorized account; current account service key for system-to-system access; developer API key only for documented app-management endpoints. OAuth, static tokens, and service keys use bearer authorization.

records.review_note: Creating a HubSpot account is self-serve and free, so the core direction is right, but the answer omits credential-specific gates. Service keys require a super admin or Developer Tools access, scopes cannot exceed the creator's object permissions, and some APIs/scopes depend on subscription tier.
records.correction: Self-serve account creation, but privileged roles are needed for service-key management and actual access is constrained by creator permissions, granted scopes, account configuration, and subscription tier.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no API-surface claim, so the rating is a forced abstention. Independent review finds date-versioned public HTTP APIs under https://api.hubapi.com, with the 2026-09 reference covering CRM and additional product APIs.
records.correction: REST/HTTP; broad multi-product HubSpot API surface, including CRM and other hubs, using date-versioned API paths and the latest version for new integrations.

records.review_note: HubSpot's own developer documentation operates the remote MCP server at https://mcp.hubspot.com. It uses OAuth with PKCE, and available tools remain limited by the user's permissions, subscription, and account configuration.
records.correction: vendor_server: HubSpot-operated remote MCP server at https://mcp.hubspot.com, authorized through OAuth with PKCE and constrained by granted permissions and account capabilities.

records.review_note: The official Composio HubSpot catalog entry lists the toolkit and its supported authentication schemes. This independently supports Composio availability only; it is not used to infer HubSpot's vendor MCP status.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a HubSpot toolkit with OAuth2/API-key authentication and managed-OAuth setup.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained, so the rating is forced. Independent evidence supports buildability through current APIs and MCP; the principal constraints are privileged credential setup, scopes, subscription-dependent access, and service-key limitations such as lack of webhook support.
records.correction: Buildable now through current HubSpot APIs or the vendor MCP; the main gates are credential role, scopes, subscription tier, endpoint access, and choosing a service key versus OAuth for required webhook behavior.

records.review_note: OAuth bearer tokens are the current recommended method and legacy API-token Basic authentication is documented, but the list does not distinguish current from retiring methods or product scope. API tokens are deprecated with staged removal through April 30, 2027; Sunshine Conversations Basic/API-key/JWT and some session methods are product-specific rather than universal Zendesk authentication.
records.correction: Prefer OAuth 2.0 access tokens with bearer authorization. Legacy API-token Basic authentication remains only until product-specific sunset dates; session authentication applies only where a Zendesk product documents it, and Sunshine Conversations API-key Basic/JWT methods are product-specific.

records.review_note: Admin-controlled API access, OAuth client configuration, and API-token management make administrator approval a common gate, but it is not universal for every Zendesk product or integration route. The answer overgeneralizes an admin-only gate.
records.correction: Admin-controlled API access and OAuth/credential setup are common gates, with exact requirements depending on the Zendesk product, authentication method, account roles, and integration model.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no API-surface claim and therefore receives a forced abstention. The official API reference documents a broad product-organized REST surface spanning Ticketing, Help Center, AI Agents, Messaging, Voice, and related services.
records.correction: REST; broad multi-product Zendesk API surface, with product-specific resources, authentication, and versioning.

records.review_note: The cited GA announcement proves a Zendesk MCP client, but client support does not prove absence of a vendor server. Zendesk separately documents its own account-specific MCP Server for Bridge/external AI agents in EAP, published October 21, 2026. The server is not GA, but it is a vendor-operated server.
records.correction: vendor_server_eap: Zendesk operates an account-specific MCP Server for Bridge/external AI agents in EAP, alongside the separate GA MCP client.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists the Zendesk toolkit with OAuth2 authentication and managed-OAuth support. This establishes Composio availability, not the state or direction of Zendesk MCP.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a Zendesk toolkit with OAuth2 authentication and managed-OAuth setup.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained, so the rating is forced. The public REST APIs support building a toolkit now with OAuth, but new implementations should avoid API-token dependencies and account for administrator configuration, product differences, and the EAP-only vendor MCP.
records.correction: Buildable now with OAuth-backed REST integrations; main constraints are product-specific API scope, admin setup, and the need to migrate away from retiring API-token methods.

records.review_note: OAuth, current access tokens sent as bearer, and narrowly scoped Basic use are supported. However, 'API token' is the ambiguous legacy custom-integration terminology rather than a clean name for current OAuth tokens, and the cited Basic method oauth.access is legacy/classic-app-only; current granular apps use oauth.v2.access. The answer does not separate these current and legacy paths.
records.correction: OAuth 2.0 plus current bot/user/app-level access tokens sent as bearer. Basic is endpoint-specific, and oauth.access is a legacy classic-app method using oauth.v2.access today; legacy custom-integration API tokens should not drive new apps.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no gate claim, so the rating is a forced abstention. Independent review finds that workspace administrator approval is conditional on workspace app-management policy, while token availability also depends on OAuth scopes and app type.
records.correction: Conditional workspace administrator approval, depending on app-management and enterprise policies, plus OAuth scope and token-type constraints; not a universal self-serve or universal admin-only gate.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no API-surface claim and receives a forced abstention. Slack explicitly documents its Web API as an HTTP RPC-style API rather than REST, with more than 200 methods and related event APIs.
records.correction: HTTP RPC-style Web API, explicitly not REST; 200+ methods plus Events API and related messaging, workflow, and administration surfaces.

records.review_note: Slack's official AI documentation operates an MCP server for Slack data and actions. This vendor evidence is independent of Composio; Slack's separate MCP-client capability does not negate the server.
records.correction: vendor_server: Slack operates an official MCP server, with Slack Agent/client support being a separate capability.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists Slack with OAuth2 authentication and managed OAuth. This verifies the Composio toolkit only and was not used as evidence for Slack's vendor MCP.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a Slack toolkit with OAuth2 authentication and managed-OAuth setup.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained and is rated accordingly. The 200+ method HTTP RPC-style Web API supports agent tooling now; the main constraints are workspace approval policy, token type, OAuth scopes, and avoiding legacy app methods.
records.correction: Buildable now using current OAuth tokens and Slack's Web/event APIs; workspace policy, OAuth scopes, token type, and legacy-method migration are the main gates.

records.review_note: The Google Ads API uses OAuth 2.0 credentials carried as bearer access tokens. The MCP's local ADC option is a separate MCP-specific path and does not contradict the standard API authentication claim.
records.correction: OAuth 2.0 access tokens sent as bearer for the Google Ads API; local ADC is an MCP-specific option.

records.review_note: Approval is materially required, but current access is managed through Google Cloud project access levels rather than merely a generic Google Ads admin approval. Enabling the API provides Test access; Explorer, Basic, and Standard have distinct review requirements, and Google Ads user roles/MCC context further constrain calls. Developer tokens were sunset on September 9, 2026.
records.correction: Google Cloud project API access-level approval plus Google Ads user roles and MCC/customer context. Enabling the API initially grants Test access; production access requires the appropriate project level.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no API-surface claim, so this is a forced abstention. Official documentation supports both REST and gRPC interfaces over a broad resource-oriented Google Ads API; the official MCP exposes only a narrower subset.
records.correction: REST and gRPC; broad Google Ads service surface covering campaigns, assets, reporting, and account operations, with a narrower MCP tool surface.

records.review_note: Google's official Google Ads Developer Toolkit documents an MCP server with local stdio and remote HTTP modes. It supports selected reporting, analysis, asset, video, and label operations rather than the full API surface.
records.correction: vendor_server: Google operates a Google Ads MCP server with local and remote modes, exposing a selected subset of Google Ads operations.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists Google Ads with OAuth2 authentication and managed OAuth. This is evidence of Composio toolkit availability only, not of Google's vendor MCP.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a Google Ads toolkit with OAuth2 authentication and managed-OAuth setup.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained, so the rating is forced. Integration is technically buildable now, but a newly enabled Cloud project initially has Test access; production use, user permissions, customer context, and project access level are the main constraints.
records.correction: Buildable now, but initial Test access limits production use until the Google Cloud project receives appropriate access; OAuth scopes, user roles, and MCC/customer context are additional gates.

records.review_note: OAuth access-token flows are supported, but the answer is incomplete and uses an outdated category. Current flows include token exchange, authorization code, and client credentials/application-only tokens. ID tokens were formerly called session tokens and authenticate the embedded user to the app backend; they are not sent to Shopify APIs and must be exchanged for access tokens.
records.correction: OAuth access-token flows plus client-credentials/application-only tokens; ID tokens (formerly session tokens) are frontend/backend user-authentication tokens exchanged for API access tokens, not direct Shopify API credentials.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no gate claim, so the rating is forced. Shopify requires merchant installation, access scopes, and in some cases Shopify approval; online-store tokens have staff-permission requirements and protected customer data can require additional approval.
records.correction: Merchant installation and scope approval, with additional Shopify approval, staff permissions, protected-customer-data approval, and special order scopes where applicable.

records.review_note: The broad commerce surface and GraphQL/REST availability are directionally right, but the answer omits the current boundary: REST Admin API became legacy on October 1, 2024, and all new public apps have had to use GraphQL Admin API exclusively since April 1, 2025. REST remains a legacy/compatibility surface, not a neutral co-equal choice for new public apps.
records.correction: Current GraphQL Admin API plus legacy/compatibility REST Admin API; broad commerce resources, but new public apps must use GraphQL exclusively.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no MCP claim and receives a forced abstention. Shopify's official page says the remote MCP is 'Coming soon' and is not publicly available yet, so it should not be described as a generally available vendor server.
records.correction: not_yet_publicly_available: Shopify has announced a remote vendor MCP server, but the official page says it is coming soon and is not publicly available yet.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists Shopify with OAuth2/S2S OAuth2 support. Managed OAuth is unavailable, so users must configure custom Shopify OAuth credentials. This does not establish the availability of Shopify's own MCP server.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a Shopify toolkit, but it requires custom Shopify OAuth credentials rather than Composio-managed OAuth.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained and is rated accordingly. Buildability is established by the current GraphQL Admin API and existing Composio toolkit, not by the still-unavailable Shopify MCP. Merchant installation, scopes, custom Composio OAuth setup, and protected-data requirements are the main constraints.
records.correction: Buildable now through GraphQL Admin API or the Composio toolkit using custom OAuth; main gates are merchant installation, access scopes, protected-data/special approvals, and custom OAuth configuration.

records.review_note: An Apify API token sent as bearer is the canonical REST authentication, and the OpenAPI query-token method is labeled API Key. The answer overstates distinct methods: API token/API key are largely interface labels here, bearer is transport, and OAuth is an option for the MCP server rather than normal REST API authentication.
records.correction: Apify API token sent as bearer for REST (recommended), with a supported but less-secure query-token method; OAuth applies to the MCP server, not the standard REST API.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no gate claim, so this is a forced abstention. Users can self-serve create personal API tokens, but organization-token management requires owner or Manage access tokens permission, and scoped tokens constrain resources and actions.
records.correction: Self-serve account and personal API-token creation; organization token management and scoped access add owner/Manage access tokens permissions and resource limits.

records.review_note: Apify API v2 is a documented RESTful HTTP API focused on Actors, runs, datasets, key-value stores, schedules, webhooks, and related platform resources. 'Moderate' appropriately scopes the breadth rather than claiming a general-purpose enterprise SaaS API.
records.correction: REST; focused/moderate API v2 surface for Actors, runs, datasets, key-value stores, schedules, webhooks, and account resources.

records.review_note: Apify documents its own hosted server at https://mcp.apify.com and a local stdio server. Remote OAuth is recommended, while an API token can instead be sent as bearer.
records.correction: vendor_server: Apify operates hosted and local MCP servers, with remote OAuth or API-token bearer authentication.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists Apify with API-key authentication and an APIFY slug. This establishes Composio availability only; Apify's vendor MCP was verified from Apify's own documentation.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes an Apify toolkit using API-key authentication.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained, so the rating is forced. The documented REST API and vendor MCP support agent tooling now. Main constraints are token scope, organization roles, private-resource authorization, file/upload handling, and platform usage limits.
records.correction: Buildable now through API v2 or the vendor MCP; token scopes, organization permissions, private-resource authorization, upload behavior, and usage limits are the main gates.

records.review_note: Basic is supported only for certain GitHub App/OAuth App endpoints using client credentials. The normal REST path is token authentication in the Authorization header, using fine-grained or classic PATs, GitHub App installation/user tokens, OAuth tokens, or GITHUB_TOKEN; username/password authentication is unsupported. Listing Basic alone is materially overbroad.
records.correction: Bearer/token authentication using PATs, GitHub App tokens, OAuth tokens, or Actions GITHUB_TOKEN; Basic client ID/secret only for specific app endpoints, never username/password.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no gate claim and receives a forced abstention. Users can create personal tokens self-serve, but organization/repository policy can require approval and GitHub Apps require installation; token scopes and private-resource access remain conditional.
records.correction: Self-serve user token creation, with conditional organization/repository approval, token-scope restrictions, and separate GitHub App installation requirements.

records.review_note: GitHub officially provides both REST and GraphQL APIs over a broad repository, issue, pull-request, Actions, security, and administration surface. Feature coverage differs by API, but the pass-12 breadth and protocol description are supported.
records.correction: REST and GraphQL; broad documented GitHub API surface, with feature coverage varying by interface.

records.review_note: GitHub's official repository documents local and remote MCP servers, including the remote endpoint https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/. Remote authentication can use OAuth or a PAT bearer token, and organization policy/toolsets constrain access.
records.correction: vendor_server: GitHub operates official local and remote MCP servers, with OAuth or PAT bearer authentication and policy/toolset restrictions.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists GitHub with OAuth2 authentication and managed OAuth. Organization approval and app installation can be additional gates, but this entry independently supports Composio availability only.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a GitHub toolkit with OAuth2 authentication and managed-OAuth setup.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained and is rated accordingly. Broad REST/GraphQL APIs and the vendor MCP make the app buildable now. The main constraints are token scopes, repository/organization policy, GitHub App installation, and private-resource approval.
records.correction: Buildable now through REST, GraphQL, or the vendor MCP; token scope, organization/repository policy, app installation, and private-resource approvals are the main gates.

records.review_note: Internal integration secrets/API tokens, PATs, and OAuth access tokens are supported and sent as bearer for API requests. The answer omits OAuth 2.0 and PATs and blurs API key versus API token versus bearer transport. Basic client authentication is limited to the OAuth token exchange/refresh endpoint.
records.correction: Internal integration API token/secret, personal access token, and OAuth 2.0 access token, all sent as bearer for API calls; Basic client credentials only at the OAuth token endpoint.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no gate claim, so the rating is forced. Internal connections require workspace-owner creation unless eligible plan/admin settings permit members, and pages/databases must be explicitly shared. Enterprise controls and guest restrictions can further limit access.
records.correction: Workspace-owner or permitted-member connection creation, enterprise/admin controls, and explicit page/database sharing; guests cannot connect to the Notion MCP.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no API-surface claim and receives a forced abstention. Notion documents an HTTPS REST API for pages, databases/data sources, blocks, comments, files, and other workspace resources, authenticated with bearer and a Notion-Version header.
records.correction: REST; broad workspace-content API covering pages, databases/data sources, blocks, comments, files, users, and search.

records.review_note: The cited page shows that Notion Agent can connect to external MCP servers, which is a client capability and does not establish absence of a Notion server. Notion separately operates a hosted remote MCP server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp with OAuth; that makes client_only factually wrong.
records.correction: vendor_server: Notion operates a hosted remote MCP server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp with OAuth; Notion Agent's support for external servers is a separate client feature.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists Notion with OAuth2/API-key authentication and managed OAuth. API-key mode uses an internal integration secret, and access remains limited to shared pages/databases; this does not determine vendor MCP status.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a Notion toolkit with OAuth2 or internal-integration API-key authentication.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained, so the rating is forced. The REST API, Composio toolkit, and vendor MCP support building now. Main constraints are connection creation permissions, resource sharing, plan/enterprise controls, and the inability of guests to connect.
records.correction: Buildable now through REST, Composio, or the vendor MCP; connection-owner permissions, page/database sharing, enterprise controls, and guest restrictions are the main gates.

records.review_note: API keys and bearer transport are valid but the answer omits OAuth 2.0 and other documented REST authentication paths. Stripe's REST API also accepts an API key as HTTP Basic username; restricted keys are recommended for most server-side use. MCP adds dated constraints: from January 11, 2027 it requires OAuth or agent API keys.
records.correction: Secret/restricted/agent API keys sent as bearer, or as the username in HTTP Basic for REST; OAuth 2.0 is also supported. Starting January 11, 2027, Stripe MCP accepts only OAuth or agent API keys.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no gate claim and receives a forced abstention. Account/key creation is self-serve, but team roles, restricted-key permissions, sandbox/live separation, MCP live/sandbox admin settings, and sensitive-action approvals add controls.
records.correction: Self-serve Stripe account/key access with role/team controls, key permissions, live/sandbox separation, MCP admin settings, and human confirmation for sensitive actions.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no API-surface claim, so the rating is forced. Stripe documents a broad resource-oriented REST API covering payments, billing, Connect, customers, products, and financial operations, typically with form-encoded requests and JSON responses.
records.correction: REST; broad payments, billing, Connect, customer, product, and financial-operations API surface.

records.review_note: Stripe operates the official MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com. It supports OAuth and agent API keys as bearer credentials; full-access secret keys and non-agent restricted keys stop working for MCP on January 11, 2027. Those future restrictions do not make the current vendor-server claim wrong.
records.correction: vendor_server: Stripe operates https://mcp.stripe.com with OAuth or agent API-key bearer authentication and a January 11, 2027 credential transition.

records.review_note: The official Composio catalog lists Stripe with API-key and OAuth2 authentication and managed OAuth. This confirms Composio availability; the REST toolkit's API-key setup must not be conflated with Stripe MCP's future agent-key requirement.
records.correction: listed: Composio publishes a Stripe toolkit with API-key or OAuth2 authentication and managed-OAuth setup.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained and is rated accordingly. Stripe is buildable now through its broad REST API, Composio, or vendor MCP. Key permissions, team controls, sensitive-action confirmation, and MCP's January 11, 2027 credential change are the principal constraints.
records.correction: Buildable now through REST, Composio, or vendor MCP; manage key permissions, team roles, human confirmation, and the 2027 MCP migration to OAuth or agent API keys.

records.review_note: Reducto documents Studio-created API keys, REDUCTO_API_KEY, and Authorization: Bearer authentication for Parse and MCP. The local MCP OAuth device-code login obtains and stores an API key; it does not establish OAuth as the normal REST API authentication method.
records.correction: API key sent as bearer for the REST API and hosted MCP; local MCP device-code OAuth is an API-key acquisition flow.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no gate claim and receives a forced abstention. Reducto offers self-serve free account creation and Studio API-key generation, with usage/credit limits and possible organization/enterprise controls depending on the account.
records.correction: Self-serve account and Studio-created API key; usage/credit limits and organization/enterprise controls may apply.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no API-surface claim, so the rating is forced. Reducto documents a focused REST/SDK document-processing surface: upload, parse, extract, split, classify, edit, pipelines, jobs, and webhooks across 30+ file types.
records.correction: REST; focused document-processing API covering upload, parse, extract, split, classify, edit, pipelines, jobs, and webhooks, with SDK support.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no MCP claim and receives a forced abstention. Reducto's own documentation establishes a hosted vendor server at https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp plus a local uvx server; this finding does not rely on Composio.
records.correction: vendor_server: Reducto operates a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp and a local uvx server, both using an API key.

records.review_note: Pass-12 made no Composio claim, so the rating is forced. The complete official Composio toolkit catalog reviewed contained 1,841 toolkits and no case-insensitive 'reducto' match; candidate /toolkits/reducto and /toolkits/reducto-ai pages also returned 404. The catalog evidence, not the 404 alone, supports non-listing.
records.correction: not_listed_in_official_catalog: Reducto did not appear in the complete official Composio toolkit catalog reviewed.

records.review_note: Pass-12 abstained, so the rating is forced. The documented REST API and vendor MCP make Reducto buildable now as an agent toolkit. Absence of a current Composio catalog entry does not block direct integration; API-key access, usage limits, and file/upload behavior are the main constraints.
records.correction: Buildable now through documented REST or the vendor MCP; main constraints are API-key access, usage/credit limits, file/upload handling, and lack of a current Composio catalog entry.
